coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available, so trial registries, regulator databases, preprint servers, patent and chemistry sources, dedicated citation graphs, and curated variant databases cannot be searched directly.
Forward- and backward-citation expansion is approximated with PubMed-linked records, author, title, target, and pathway searches; citation-graph completeness cannot be established.
PubMed indexing and abstract availability may underrepresent very recent, non-English, historical linkage, and conference evidence.
Variant classification and population-frequency assertions cannot be independently reconciled against ClinVar, gnomAD, locus-specific databases, or ancestry-focused genomic resources.
The source restriction limits direct verification of unpublished null findings and current clinical or regulatory status of LRRK2-targeted interventions.
exclusion_criteria: Records mentioning LRRK2 only in an undifferentiated gene list without variant-level, mechanistic, substrate, or disease-relevant analysis.
Studies focused on another disorder without an explicit analysis of Parkinson disease relevance or an LRRK2 mechanism transferable to the question.
Purely computational predictions lacking genetic, biochemical, cellular, structural, or in vivo validation.
Biomarker association reports that cannot distinguish LRRK2 genotype, kinase activity, or a traceable downstream substrate readout.
Drug efficacy reports without evidence bearing on LRRK2 target engagement, mechanism, substrate phosphorylation, or the strength of the proposed disease mechanism.
Conference abstracts, editorials, and narrative commentary lacking unique data, except when used solely to locate a primary record.
Duplicate canonical records are excluded from duplicate counting while every query-to-record occurrence and corrected version link is retained.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date is on or before 2024-12-31 after resolving online-first, issue, correction, and indexing-date ambiguity.

The record reports primary human genetic evidence, biochemical or structural mechanism, physiological substrate evidence, disease-relevant perturbation evidence, or a review used to locate and contextualize such primary studies.
The study directly concerns LRRK2 or PARK8 and Parkinson disease, or tests an LRRK2 molecular mechanism with clear relevance to the disease relationship.
Human studies report identifiable variants, association or segregation methods, ancestry or population context, and interpretable disease outcomes.
Mechanistic studies specify the LRRK2 construct or variant, assay system, perturbation, substrate or readout, and relevant controls.
Cellular and animal studies are retained when organism, tissue or cell type, genotype, and relationship to human disease are explicit.
Null, negative, conflicting, replication, correction, and retraction records are eligible when they bear on a major genetic or mechanistic claim.
English full-text records and non-English records with an English abstract are eligible when sufficient methods and findings can be assessed.

queries.purpose: Recover the PARK8 linkage and 2004 LRRK2 mutation-discovery anchor literature while validating target aliases and disease terminology.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract]) AND (Parkinson*[Title/Abstract] OR "Parkinson Disease"[MeSH Terms]) AND (linkage[Title/Abstract] OR mutation*[Title/Abstract] OR "autosomal dominant"[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

queries.purpose: Retrieve the broad human genetic-discovery record, including linkage, cloning, segregation, and founder evidence.
queries.query: (("Leucine-Rich Repeat Serine-Threonine Protein Kinase-2"[MeSH Terms] OR LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Parkinson Disease"[MeSH Terms] OR Parkinson*[Title/Abstract]) AND (genetic*[Title/Abstract] OR linkage[Title/Abstract] OR segregation[Title/Abstract] OR mutation*[Title/Abstract] OR "positional cloning"[Title/Abstract] OR founder[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

queries.purpose: Find evidence that weakens causal, universal gain-of-function, substrate, or model-based interpretations, including nonpenetrance and discordant perturbation results.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract]) AND (Parkinson*[Title/Abstract] OR kinase[Title/Abstract] OR GTPase[Title/Abstract] OR Rab[Title/Abstract]) AND ("negative result"[Title/Abstract] OR "null result"[Title/Abstract] OR nonpenetran*[Title/Abstract] OR "incomplete penetrance"[Title/Abstract] OR replication[Title/Abstract] OR inconsistent[Title/Abstract] OR discordant[Title/Abstract] OR "loss of function"[Title/Abstract] OR knockout[Title/Abstract] OR inhibitor*[Title/Abstract] OR limitation*[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

queries.purpose: Identify corrections, errata, and retractions that could alter high-impact genetic or mechanistic claims.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract]) AND (Parkinson*[Title/Abstract] OR Rab[Title/Abstract] OR kinase[Title/Abstract]) AND (Retracted Publication[Publication Type] OR Retraction of Publication[Publication Type] OR Corrected and Republished Article[Publication Type] OR correction[Title] OR erratum[Title] OR retraction[Title])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

queries.purpose: Capture recent genetic, substrate, and mechanistic updates through the delivery cutoff after the earlier waves are merged.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract]) AND (Parkinson*[Title/Abstract] OR "Parkinson Disease"[MeSH Terms]) AND (variant*[Title/Abstract] OR penetrance[Title/Abstract] OR kinase[Title/Abstract] OR GTPase[Title/Abstract] OR Rab[Title/Abstract] OR substrate*[Title/Abstract] OR mechanism*[Title/Abstract])) AND ("2023/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: through 2024-12-31, identify human genetic discovery and disease-associated LRRK2 variants in Parkinson disease, connect variant-specific effects to kinase and ROC-COR GTPase regulation and physiological substrates, and assess human, cellular, biochemical, and animal evidence that supports or limits causal strength, penetrance, population generality, and model transferability. Include peer-reviewed English-language primary studies, systematic reviews, and authoritative mechanistic reviews; retain non-English records with an English abstract when they contain unique primary human genetic evidence.
stop_rules: Complete all twelve planned PubMed query events and record each exact query, execution timestamp, publication cutoff, result count, and available provider version.
The sentinel wave must recover the PARK8 linkage and independent 2004 LRRK2 mutation-discovery anchor study families; expand aliases and rerun the affected query if either family is absent.

Continue confirmation until evidence has been retrieved for genetic discovery, major pathogenic variants, ancestry-associated risk variants, kinase and ROC-COR mechanism, and Rab substrate phosphorylation.
Continue the challenge wave until searches cover incomplete penetrance, population heterogeneity, discordant or null perturbation evidence, model limitations, corrections, and retractions.
Deduplicate by PMID, DOI, and study identity while preserving all query-to-record links; conflicting metadata or results under one identifier trigger manual reconciliation and fail-closed handling.
Stop iterative term expansion after two consecutive expansion passes add no new decision-relevant study family, variant class, substrate class, or material counterevidence.

Apply the 2024-12-31 cutoff after retrieval when PubMed date fields are ambiguous, and stop the update wave only after all eligible online-first and correction records through that date are reconciled.

If the twelve-event budget is exhausted before anchor recovery or required evidence domains are covered, stop and report the unmet domain as a coverage gap rather than silently narrowing the question.
